generatedCommentsNodes.comment: In `checkAndResetDestinationIndexBlock`, the variable `currentIndex` is set to `null` if `getIndexer()` returns `null`. However, this method does not handle the case where `getIndexer().getConfig()` might return `null`. It would be safer to add a null check for `getIndexer().getConfig()` before accessing its `getDestination().getIndex()`.
The method `changesDestIndex` uses a negation (`== false`) to check for inequality, which can be simplified by directly using `!=`. This makes the logic clearer and more concise.

The test `testChangesDestIndex` is comprehensive and covers different scenarios. However, it could benefit from more descriptive variable names to improve readability. For example, `newDestWithSameIndex` and `newDestWithNewIndex` are clear, but `config` and `update` could be renamed to `originalConfig` and `updatedConfig` respectively for better clarity.

review_comment: I don't know the code base well but is it possible for the nested objects to be null too? Or only the result of `getIndexer()`?

Only the result of `getIndexer()`:
- indexer verifies that [config](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/x-pack/plugin/transform/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/transform/transforms/TransformIndexer.java#L160) is non null
- [destination](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/x-pack/plugin/core/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/core/transform/transforms/TransformConfig.java#L230) does too
- [index](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/x-pack/plugin/core/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/core/transform/transforms/DestConfig.java#L60) does too
